newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Focus on data, Boskin report.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Focus on data, Boskin report.

text.p: U.S. credit markets will focus on two main points Wednesday: some fresh economic data and the release of the final report of the Senate Finance Committee's bipartisan commission on the consumer price index.

Analysts said players are somewhat anxious ahead of the release of the Committee's report. A preliminary version of the document released in September said the CPI overstates consumer inflation between 0.7 and 2.0 percent.

"I think it's going to be an important event in the sense that it will focus so much attention on this question of the overstatement of inflation," said William Griggs, managing director of consulting firm Griggs and Santow Inc.

The initial estimate of the commission, chaired by Stanford economist Michael Boskin, was that the CPI may be overstated by 1.0 percent. But more precise calculations were left for the final report, scheduled to be released Wednesday.
The ideas proposed by the so-called Boskin committee may or may not be implemented by the government. But money market traders said they like what they have seen so far.

"An overstated CPI could actually be forcing the government to spend much more than it should," said a trader at a U.S. investment bank. "If that stops, it may become easier for the government to reduce its debt."
The trader was referring to the fact that payments of many government benefits, including social security adjustments, are pegged to the variation of the CPI.
Some analysts, however, were skeptical about the possible implementations of the ideas proposed in the report.
"I would think it's pretty unlikely that this commission's recommendations will be adopted in full," said Lee Youngdahl, economist and vice-president at Aubrey G. Lanston and Co. Inc.
"It's going to be food for thought and a lot of fodder for the politicians going forward, but I would not expect any kind of a near-term push from it."
The market will also take in the Federal Reserve's Beige Book, which is expected to be released at 1200 EST/1700 GMT.
In a nutshell, analysts expect the report to show moderate economic growth and restrained price pressures.

"One caveat is that the labor markets remain tight. This has been alluded by several Fed officials recently...but yet they don't see that translating into higher prices. They're just at this point keeping an eye on it," Youngdahl added.
On the technical front, analysts said the underlying trend for the market remains bullish, with the next target for the benchmark 30-year bond yield seen at 6.25 percent.
On Tuesday, the Treasury long bond was quoted up 2/32 at 101-29/32 in late trading to yield 6.36 percent.

The Federal Reserve added temporary reserves to the money market on Tuesday through overnight system repurchase agreements when federal funds funds were traded at 5-7/16 percent, well above the central bank's 5-1/4 percent target.

The market was somewhat disappointed as the Fed decided to refrain from adding permanent reserves to the system through a coupon pass operation on Tuesday. Analysts said the operation is still likely to take place on Wednesday though.
